hyperedges.label: AST + Semantic Extraction and Merge Pipeline

nodes.label: Interpreter Guard for Subcommands
nodes.rationale: Subcommands can run after the user deleted graphify-out/, so the interpreter marker must be re-resolved before any subcommand rather than assumed present.

nodes.label: .graphify_python Interpreter Marker
nodes.rationale: Written once at install time so every subsequent bash block uses the same interpreter across invocations (uv tool, pipx, venv, or system install).

nodes.label: --update (Incremental Re-extraction)
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new or changed files to save tokens and time.

nodes.label: --cluster-only
nodes.rationale: Reruns clustering on the existing graph without re-extraction.

nodes.label: /graphify query Flow
nodes.rationale: When graph.json already exists, answering from the graph avoids rebuilding the corpus for every question.

nodes.label: Question Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: The question is expanded against the graph's own vocabulary before traversal so a wording mismatch does not collapse the answer to noise.

nodes.label: Inline NetworkX Traversal Fallback
nodes.rationale: Used when the graphify query CLI is unavailable, so a missing CLI does not block answering.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge; use AMBIGUOUS when unsure. Always show token cost, never hide cohesion behind symbols, and warn before HTML viz above 5,000 nodes.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Aider Variant)
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph; treats codebase questions as graphify queries first when graphify-out/ exists.

nodes.label: Step 1 - Ensure graphify Installed
nodes.rationale: Interpreter detection tries uv tool first (most reliable on modern Mac/Linux), then the graphify binary shebang for pipx/pip installs, then falls back to python3.

nodes.label: Step 2 - Detect Files
nodes.rationale: The detect JSON is read silently rather than printed so the user sees a clean corpus summary; skipped_sensitive files are listed so a wrongly-flagged source is visible and can be renamed (#2106).

nodes.label: Step 2.5 - Transcribe Video/Audio
nodes.rationale: Video and audio cannot be read directly, so they are transcribed to text and then treated as doc files. The agent writes the Whisper domain hint itself from god node labels because it is already a language model — no separate API call needed.

nodes.label: GRAPHIFY_WHISPER_PROMPT Domain Hint
nodes.rationale: A domain hint composed from top god node labels improves transcription; a video-only corpus has no labels to draw on, so it falls back to a generic punctuation prompt.

nodes.label: Step 3 - Extract Entities and Relationships
nodes.rationale: Split into deterministic free AST extraction and token-costing semantic extraction; the two run in parallel because they operate on different file types, saving 5-15s on large corpora.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Rule
nodes.rationale: Code is extracted structurally via AST with no LLM at all, and semantic extraction uses the host agent's own model; graphify never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, so prompting for or blocking on a key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: Part A - Structural AST Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free; always writes .graphify_ast.json even with no code files so the downstream merge has its input.
nodes.source_location: #### Part A - Structural extraction for code files

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction
nodes.rationale: Skipped entirely for a code-only corpus because AST already covers code. On Aider extraction runs sequentially since multi-agent support is early — slower than parallel platforms but fully reliable.

nodes.label: Step B0 - Semantic Cache Check
nodes.rationale: Only document/paper/image categories go to semantic extraction — flattening every category would make the step re-read every source file already covered by AST (#1392). The cache file is deleted when empty so Part C never merges a stale .graphify_cached.json.

nodes.label: Step B1 - Split into Chunks
nodes.rationale: Chunks of 20-25 files, one chunk per image because vision needs separate context; files from the same directory are grouped so cross-file relationships are more likely to be extracted.

nodes.label: Step B2 - Sequential Extraction (Aider)
nodes.rationale: Aider's early multi-agent support means files are processed one at a time by the host model itself.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS Confidence Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Every edge is tagged so the user can tell what was found versus invented — this is the honest audit trail. EXTRACTED=1.0, INFERRED=0.6-0.9 reasoned individually, AMBIGUOUS=0.1-0.3; uncertain edges are flagged, never omitted.

nodes.label: file_type Enumeration
nodes.rationale: Must be exactly one of code, document, paper, image, rationale, concept; rationale is stored as a node attribute rather than a separate node.

nodes.label: Hyperedge Rule
nodes.rationale: Added only when 3+ nodes share a concept or flow not already captured by pairwise edges, max 3 per file, so hyperedges carry information rather than duplicating edges.

nodes.label: Step B3 - Cache and Merge Chunks
nodes.rationale: Real token counts are read from the Agent result usage field and written back into the chunk JSON before merging because the chunk JSON always carries placeholder zeros. If more than half the chunks fail, stop and tell the user.

nodes.label: Part C - Merge AST + Semantic
nodes.rationale: AST nodes go in first and semantic nodes are deduplicated by id against them, so deterministic structural nodes win over inferred ones.

nodes.label: Step 4 - Build, Cluster, Analyze, Output
nodes.source_location: ### Step 4 - Build graph, cluster, analyze, generate outputs

nodes.label: Empty-Graph Write Guard
nodes.rationale: Checked immediately after build and before any write, because an empty extraction must not clobber a good graph.json, GRAPH_REPORT.md, or analysis sidecar (#1392).

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard (#479)
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to overwrite graph.json with fewer nodes than the existing graph; the report is written only after the graph actually persisted, because a report describing a graph that was not written would be a lie (#1392).

nodes.label: --directed / IS_DIRECTED Substitution
nodes.rationale: True builds a DiGraph preserving edge direction source->target; False (default) builds an undirected Graph. The literal placeholder must be substituted everywhere it appears.

nodes.label: graphify.analyze.surprising_connections
nodes.rationale: Community detection surfaces connections between concepts in different files the user would never think to ask about directly.

nodes.label: graphify.analyze.suggest_questions
nodes.rationale: Regenerated in Step 5 with real community labels because labels affect question phrasing.

nodes.label: Step 5 - Label Communities
nodes.rationale: The agent writes 2-5 word plain-language names, then graph.json is re-exported so its nodes carry the curated community_name (#2490); the same extraction is used so the #479 shrink guard passes on node count.

nodes.label: Step 6 - Obsidian Vault + HTML
nodes.rationale: HTML is generated always unless --no-viz; the Obsidian vault is opt-in because it generates one file per node. Graphs above 5,000 nodes are too large for HTML viz and are directed to the vault instead.

nodes.label: graphify.export.to_canvas
nodes.rationale: Gives Obsidian a structured community layout with communities as groups.

nodes.label: Step 7 - Neo4j Export/Push
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so re-running the push is safe and does not create duplicates.

nodes.label: graphify.export.to_svg
nodes.rationale: SVG embeds in Obsidian, Notion, and GitHub READMEs.

nodes.label: graphify.export.to_graphml
nodes.rationale: GraphML opens in Gephi, yEd, or any GraphML tool.

nodes.label: Step 7d - MCP stdio Server (graphify.serve)
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats, and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live.

nodes.label: Step 8 - Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Skipped silently below 5,000 words because for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Step 9 - Manifest, Cost Tracker, Cleanup, Report
graphify.cli._stamped_manifest_files
nodes.rationale: Only semantic files that actually produced output are stamped, so a failed chunk is re-queued on the next run rather than silently lost (#2015).

nodes.label: Cumulative Cost Tracker (cost.json)
nodes.rationale: Accumulates per-run and all-time input/output token counts so token cost is always visible, per the honesty rules.

nodes.label: Be the Guide After the Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Only God Nodes, Surprising Connections, and Suggested Questions are pasted into chat to keep it concise; the agent then offers the single most boundary-crossing question so the session feels like navigation rather than a one-shot report. The graph is the map, the agent is the guide.

nodes.label: --update Incremental Flow
nodes.rationale: Only re-extracts changed files to save tokens and time; a code-only change set skips semantic extraction entirely because no LLM is needed.

nodes.label: Empty Extraction for Deletion-Only Updates
nodes.rationale: When only deletions occurred there are no new files, so an empty extraction file is written to give the merge step something to prune against.

nodes.label: graphify.analyze.graph_diff
nodes.rationale: Compares the pre-merge backup (.graphify_old.json) against the new extraction to show what the update added.

nodes.label: --cluster-only Flow
nodes.rationale: Skips Steps 1-3 and re-clusters the existing graph.json. graph.json is exported without community_labels here because labels are still placeholders; Step 5 re-exports with the curated names (#2490).

nodes.label: /graphify query Traversal
nodes.rationale: Answers strictly from what the graph contains and quotes source_location when citing a fact; if the graph lacks information the agent says so rather than hallucinating edges.

nodes.label: BFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode; explores neighbors layer by layer to depth 3, best for 'what is X connected to' broad-context questions.

nodes.label: DFS Traversal Mode (--dfs)
nodes.rationale: Follows one path as deep as possible before backtracking, depth-limited to 6 to avoid traversing the whole graph; best for tracing a specific chain or dependency path.

nodes.label: --budget Token Cap
nodes.rationale: Nodes are ranked by term-overlap relevance and output is cut at roughly 4 chars per token, so the most relevant subgraph survives truncation.

nodes.label: graphify save-result Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: Saves the Q&A back into the graph so the next --update extracts it as a node, closing the feedback loop and improving future queries.

nodes.label: /graphify explain (Node Explanation)
nodes.rationale: Lists everything connected to one node with relations, confidence tags, and source files, which the agent turns into a 3-5 sentence explanation citing source locations.

nodes.label: graph.json Existence Precheck
nodes.rationale: Every read-side subcommand stops with a clear instruction to run /graphify <path> first rather than failing obscurely on a missing graph.

nodes.label: /graphify add (URL Ingest)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects Twitter/X (oEmbed), arXiv, PDF, images, and generic webpages (html2text); on error it tells the user rather than silently continuing, and on success it auto-runs --update on ./raw.

nodes.label: --watch Auto-Rebuild Watcher
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; docs/papers/images only write a needs_update flag because they require LLM semantic re-extraction. Debounce waits until file activity stops so a wave of parallel agent writes does not trigger a rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit with no background process and works with any editor; it appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it. Doc/image changes are ignored because they need a manual --update.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: Run once per project so Claude checks the graph before answering codebase questions and rebuilds after code changes, removing the need for a manual /graphify in future sessions.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules (Aider)
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge (use AMBIGUOUS), never skip the corpus check warning, always show token cost, show raw cohesion numbers rather than symbols, and warn before HTML viz above 5,000 nodes.

nodes.label: graphify Skill (Claw Variant)
nodes.rationale: Same skill contract as the Aider variant but for a host that can dispatch parallel subagents and clone GitHub URLs.

nodes.label: Fast Path - Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: If graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language codebase question rather than an explicit rebuild, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely and the query runs immediately — the graph is already built, so re-detecting or asking the user to narrow is wasted work.

nodes.label: Step 0 - GitHub Clone and Multi-Path Merge
nodes.rationale: Runs only for github.com URLs or several local subfolders to merge into one cross-repo graph; a plain local path skips it.

nodes.label: .graphify_root Scan Root Marker
nodes.rationale: Saves the resolved scan root so a bare `graphify update` with no arguments knows where to look next time.

nodes.label: Python-Written Detect Sidecar (#2528)
nodes.rationale: The detect sidecar is written from Python with explicit UTF-8 rather than a shell redirect so the same block renders correctly on PowerShell hosts without console-encoding drift (#2528).

nodes.label: Corpus Size Warning and Subfolder Narrowing
nodes.rationale: Above 2,000,000 words or 500 files the top 5 first-level subdirectories are offered; graphify-out sidecars are filtered out of the ranking, and if everything is at the root there are no subfolders to narrow to, so --no-cluster is suggested instead.

nodes.label: Gemini Semantic Extraction Backend
nodes.rationale: Used only if GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY is already set, replacing subagent dispatch; the tip is printed once and never blocks, because the host agent itself is the LLM when no key exists. Default model gemini-3-flash-preview, overridable via GRAPHIFY_GEMINI_MODEL or --model.

nodes.label: Empty Semantic File for Code-Only Corpus
nodes.rationale: Part C reads .graphify_semantic.json unconditionally, so a code-only run must write an empty one or the merge hits FileNotFoundError.

nodes.label: Mandatory Parallel Agent Dispatch
nodes.rationale: Reading files one-by-one is 5-10x slower than subagents. All Agent calls must go out in a single message or they run sequentially and defeat the purpose.

nodes.label: general-purpose Subagent Type Requirement
nodes.rationale: Explore is read-only and cannot write chunk files to disk, which silently drops extraction results; general-purpose has the Write and Bash access the subagent needs.

nodes.label: references/extraction-spec.md as Cache Key (#1939)
nodes.rationale: The spec is the extraction prompt, so cache entries are attributed to it: a graphify upgrade that changes the prompt forces re-extraction of entries produced by the old one, while an unchanged prompt keeps its entries (#1939). The same absolute path must be passed to both B0 and B3.

nodes.label: Pre-Dispatch Timing Estimate
nodes.rationale: Agents needed is ceil(uncached non-code files / 22) at ~45s per parallel batch, printed so the user knows the expected wait before dispatch.

nodes.label: Absolute CHUNK_PATH from cwd (#1392)
nodes.rationale: Derived from the current working directory where Part C globs graphify-out/, not from .graphify_root or the scan directory, or the merge finds no chunks (#1392).

nodes.label: --wiki Agent-Crawlable Wiki
nodes.rationale: Builds index.md plus one article per community.

nodes.label: --obsidian-dir Custom Vault Path
nodes.rationale: Lets the vault be written into an existing Obsidian vault instead of graphify-out/.

nodes.label: --help Prints Usage Verbatim
nodes.rationale: With --help and no other arguments, print the Usage block and stop — no commands, no detection, no defaulting the path to '.', so asking for help never triggers an expensive build.
nodes.source_location: ## What You Must Do When Invoked

nodes.label: Persistent Cross-Session Graph
nodes.rationale: Relationships are stored in graphify-out/graph.json and survive across sessions, so questions can be asked weeks later without re-reading everything.

nodes.label: Karpathy /raw Folder Workflow
nodes.rationale: Drop anything — papers, tweets, screenshots, code, notes — into one folder and get a structured graph that shows what you didn't know was connected.
